facts.label: Emblematic dish
facts.value: Gozo is named among the emblematic dishes of Bangui, with fish maboké and fufu with okra

facts.label: Daily lunch
facts.value: A Bangui resident describes the cassava eaten at lunch with yetoum leaves and groundnut meat as 'gozo', a flagship dish never missing from the lunch table

facts.label: Change
facts.value: Many young people pay little attention to these traditional dishes and prefer Western food

facts.label: Base crop
facts.value: Cassava, the base of gozo, supplies about half of food energy needs in the Central African Republic (FAO figure for CAR, Congo and Zaire)

facts.label: Processing
facts.value: Cassava is the population's main staple; it is processed by peeling, retting (soaking to detoxify the tubers) and drying

facts.label: Kanda
facts.value: Kanda is a Central African Republic speciality of seasoned, fried minced-meat balls simmered in a sauce of ground pumpkin seeds and fresh tomatoes

facts.label: Kanda served with
facts.value: Kanda is often served with fufu, cassava or rice

parts.text: Gozo is the cassava staple of Central African meals and is named among the emblematic dishes of Bangui; cassava, peeled, retted to remove toxins and dried, supplies about half of the country's food energy. Kanda is a Central African speciality of seasoned, fried meatballs simmered in a sauce of ground pumpkin seeds and tomatoes.
Gozo is a lunchtime staple eaten with leaf and groundnut sauces, and kanda is often served with fufu, cassava or rice.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
